title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County, 21-year-old Jaclynn Gonzales and her 12-year-old sister, have sued the city of Española over a July 23 traffic stop. A Flock Safety surveillance camera misread their license plate, changing the final digit from 2 to 7, and flagged the car as stolen in Rio Rancho. Officers stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed both sisters, and placed them in separate police vehicles. Jaclynn asked police to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the 12-year-old and put her in a police car.

The lawsuits, filed Jan. 3, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, worry, and restriction of movement. Their attorney, Sheri Raphaelson, also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was mistakenly stopped in a similar case in April. The city, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The cases are now pending in state District Court.
